picks.why: The synthesis calls this my clearest case: it trades at 19.4x trailing earnings, which grew 52.8%, it beat Q2 and got a $691 target from Citi, yet it fell 6.83% to $525.28 on 10-year yields rather than anything in the business, which puts it at the watchlist's $520 add zone with a $500 stop.

At 11.6x trailing with earnings still up 10.1% and no quarterly report until 10-14, the best underwriter on the sheet is priced like an average insurer, and a 10-year above 4.75% raises the income on its bond portfolio instead of compressing its multiple.

At 16.5x trailing with earnings up 6.2% and 1.89% weekly volatility, it is in my real-yield basket and passes the Campbell test because earnings are still growing, unlike the costly defensives COST at 46.1x and WMT at 37.9x.

It is the one name from my MO/PM/KMB preference on the sheet: 22.5x trailing is backed by 14.7% earnings growth, it screened cheap against the rising 10-year, and it held up better than the bond-like staples in last week's selloff.

At 16.5x trailing with earnings up 13.4% and almost the lowest volatility on the sheet (1.52% weekly), it is the sound big-bank way to own the interest-income boost that lifted WFC and C last week, and it partly hedges the hot-CPI risk.

summary: With CPI due on 9-11 and the 10-year above 4.75%, I owned cheap, sound businesses whose earnings are still growing and don't depend on falling rates: one stock sold down on yields alone (LMT), two that gain from higher-for-longer rates (PGR, JPM) and two high-yield staples that pass the Campbell test (PEP, PM). I passed on names that are cheap but shrinking (STZ, CALM, HON, VICI), on crude at $91, on the momentum and AI names at chase prices, and on FIZZ, which reports this week. I have no memory of how this week went and used none.
